clue.text: Meal apt to be laid out round about here?

definitions.text: Meal apt to be laid out round about here?

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for about
laid out suggests arranging things anew, so the letters of meal and apt are rearranged

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether this is the spot where the food is about to be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be laid out' makes PLAEMAT, and 'round' wraps it about the circa abbreviation; read whole, the clue also describes the item where a meal is set.
explanation.definitionFit: A table mat is exactly where a diner's meal is set down, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: How long to prepare metal item for forging?

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal

indicators.note: forging means shaping metal anew, so the letters of item are reworked

explanation.surface: A smith asks how long it will take to get a metal piece ready for the forge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for forging' is the anagram signal, its rearranged letters giving the second word of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead time is the interval needed to get ready before production or delivery.

clue.text: Recording ready, one may advise change

definitions.text: Recording ready, one may advise change

parts.words: Recording ready, one may advise change
parts.note: ready is slang for cash, so a machine that records ready money and tells the cashier how much change to give

explanation.surface: A broadcaster set to record warns that things may be about to change.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop till records the cash taken and displays the change owed to a customer.

clue.text: Clear chap is gripping iron on tee

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: gripping means holding something inside, so is wraps round the iron symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the letter T is spelt tee

explanation.surface: A golfer holds an iron above the ball sitting on its tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' is the container signal; 'on' simply places the final letter after the rest in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest as an adjective means obvious or plain to see.

clue.text: Industry relocating people currently out of work?

definitions.text: Industry relocating people currently out of work?

parts.words: Industry relocating people currently out of work?
parts.note: people on holiday are temporarily away from their jobs, and a whole trade moves them about

explanation.surface: A business moves unemployed workers to new places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of work' suggests the jobless, but here it means people on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The holiday trade is an industry that moves holidaymakers, who are away from their jobs, around.

clue.text: Stood up, going over to catch name under Conservative banner

indicators.note: to catch means to hold inside, so the name abbreviation sits within the word for stood up
going over means turning over, so the whole piece reads backwards up the column

parts.note: rose means stood up

explanation.surface: Protesters rose to their feet, crossing over to grab a name under a Tory banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to catch' puts N inside ROSE giving ROSNE; 'going over' turns that to ENSOR, set 'under' C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bans things is jokingly a banner, as an official who suppresses material does.

clue.text: Head away from trail that's hopeless

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: spoor is the trail left by an animal

explanation.surface: A tracker who heads off the trail is a lost cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head away from' drops the first letter S from SPOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor can mean weak or of low quality, so a hopeless effort is a poor one.

clue.text: Debris? It's gathered in by flapping duster

indicators.note: gathered in by means held inside the following piece
flapping a duster sends it every which way, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dust is collected by shaking a duster about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapping' gives DETRUS, which 'gathered in by' wraps around the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus means loose waste matter or rubble, a synonym of debris.

clue.text: Description of eleven's encounter

parts.note: the figures 11 show a one placed beside another one, and also a meeting of just two individuals

explanation.surface: A football team's match is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eleven' suggests a team, but the numeral 11 is simply one digit next to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-to-one meeting involves just two people face to face, and 11 is a pair of ones.

clue.text: Mountain route not entirely abandoned?

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: ...é means out of fashion, dropped or abandoned

explanation.surface: A mountain trail is not quite deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final E from PASSE (out of date, given up).
explanation.definitionFit: A pass is a gap or track through a range of hills or mountains.

clue.text: Whereby one attempts to recapture the effect of a shock?

definitions.text: Whereby one attempts to recapture the effect of a shock?

parts.words: Whereby one attempts to recapture the effect of a shock?
parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass, so this is a product meant to regrow a full head of hair

explanation.surface: Someone tries to relive the thrill of a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like a fright, but a shock is a mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic for baldness aims to bring back a thick head of hair, a shock.

clue.text: A source of unfair advantage? Nothing cold and hostile aroused

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so the letters of cold and hostile are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone resents a cold, hostile response to an unfair privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aroused' is the anagram signal; the zero letter stands in front of the rearranged pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Neckwear of a former school stands for the network of contacts that gives favours to old pupils.

clue.text: Muses about Church Council's description

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so nine goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: there were nine Muses in Greek myth
CE is short for Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone ponders the description of a church council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muses' looks like a verb, but it stands for NINE, the number of Muses; 'about' puts it around CE.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the Council of Nicaea, as in the creed adopted there.

clue.text: Noisy leader from Stoke-on- Trent? I had to intervene

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word that follows
to intervene means to come between, so the short form of I had goes inside the river's name

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A loud-voiced figure leads the way in Stoke-on-Trent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader from' gives S; 'to intervene' sends the contraction inside the Staffordshire river's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and harsh-sounding, a synonym of noisy.

clue.text: No time to think for referee

indicators.note: no says a letter is taken away

parts.note: to meditate is to think deeply

explanation.surface: A referee gets no time to think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes T (time) from MEDITATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to act as a go-between in a dispute, as a referee does.

clue.text: Work on nails -cracked, and certain to be without tip

parts.note: cracked means crazy, as does manic

indicators.note: without its tip means losing the first letter

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A carpenter's nails have cracked, though he is sure the job is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked' hints at broken nails but means crazy; 'to be without tip' drops S from SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicure is a cosmetic treatment of the fingernails.

clue.text: Second in field event provokes debate

indicators.note: in says the second's abbreviation is set inside the event

parts.note: the discus is an athletics field event

explanation.surface: A runner-up in an athletics event causes argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside DISCUS, between its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss a matter is to talk it over or debate it.

clue.text: Mischief-maker definitely not turning up in jail

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: no sir is an emphatic refusal

explanation.surface: A troublemaker who refuses to appear ends up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives RISON, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison someone is to put them in jail; both work as verbs.

clue.text: Film treatment, thus involves translation of Racine

indicators.note: involves means holds within, so the word for thus wraps round the rest

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: translation here means changing the form, so the letters of Racine are rearranged

explanation.surface: A screenwriter adapts a play by the French dramatist Racine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' gives CENARI, the dramatist's name rearranged, which 'involves' sets within the two-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a written outline of a film's plot, a treatment.

clue.text: Author's seen vehicle turn

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the author is the definition

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a roll is a turn over

explanation.surface: A writer has been spotted turning a car over.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis Carroll wrote the Alice books.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of the writer of Alice in Wonderland.

clue.text: Expanse of water another's polluted

indicators.note: polluted means fouled or corrupted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stretch of water belonging to someone else is contaminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polluted' rearranges ANOTHERS, keeping the S of the 's.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea between Britain and Scandinavia is a large body of water.

clue.text: Monkey, say, intent on taking the rise in misbehaving

indicators.note: in says one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing, misbehaving

indicators.note: taking the rise in a down clue means going upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: an aim is an intent

explanation.surface: A monkey mocking people while misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking the rise' reverses AIM to MIA, which goes 'in' SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Simian means a monkey or ape; 'say' marks a monkey as one example.

clue.text: No Stranger on the Shore from piano fan!

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a lover is a devotee or fan

explanation.surface: A pianist who loves the hit tune Stranger on the Shore plays it.
explanation.walkthrough: Stranger on the Shore was a 1961 Acker Bilk hit; the bird is a familiar sight on beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: This wading bird is a common sight on beaches, so it is no stranger there.

clue.text: Roman poet following attempt to win in tribunal

parts.note: to court is to try to win someone's favour
Martial was a Roman writer of epigrams

explanation.surface: A Roman poet is tried before a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: Martial wrote short witty epigrams in first-century Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A military court trying service members is a kind of tribunal.

clue.text: Element of munitions squad

indicators.note: element of means part of the word munitions, whose letters contain the answer

explanation.surface: Part of a weapons squad's equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element of' shows the letters lie within munitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a small group of soldiers, such as a squad.

clue.text: Sharp's pack of cards having nothing missing

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so sharp alone is the definition

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a tarot is a pack of fortune-telling cards
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A card sharp has a pack with nothing missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes O (nothing) out of TAROT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart describes a sharp, acid taste.

clue.text: Climate measure, one representing sun in autumn

parts.note: Ra was the Egyptian god of the sun
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Meteorologists measure the climate when the sun shines in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall, the amount of precipitation, is a standard measurement of climate.

clue.text: Knight's path and destiny lying round front of castle

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so knight alone is the definition

indicators.note: lying round means surrounding, so the path goes around the front letter

parts.note: a lane is a path

indicators.note: front of means the first letter

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A knight's way and fate encircle a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' picks C, and 'lying round' has the path enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot was the most famous knight of King Arthur's Round Table.
